This figure is from AC 43.13-1B, Acceptable Methods, Techniques, and Practices: Aircraft Inspection and Repair, chapter 7 (aircraft hardware, control cables, and turnbuckles). Its caption: "FIGURE 7-7. Alternate method for securing with cotter pins.".
Describe it for a mechanic who can't see it: say what it shows, then transcribe every label,
value, unit, part number, and note printed in it. Don't add anything that isn't in the figure.
If it shows nothing of use (a logo, a signature, a blank area), say so in one sentence.

message.content:
The figure shows two diagrams illustrating an alternate method for securing with cotter pins. On the left, a circular component with a central shaft is shown with two 60° angles marked, indicating the range of motion or positioning for a cotter pin installation, with a label pointing to the head of the component stating "HEAD SNUG TO SHANK." On the right, a detailed view of a mechanical assembly, likely a turnbuckle or similar hardware, is labeled "ALTERNATE."

- 60°
- 60°
- HEAD SNUG TO SHANK
- ALTERNATE
